answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may trade, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove collusion or fabricated transactions. A cedar-backed reputation record can carry verified delivery history across markets, while a juniper review window delays withdrawals until disputes settle. Splitting into many identities then multiplies the capital locked and the risk of forfeiture; a ripple of coordinated trades cannot create trustworthy history for free.
